identity.name: Turco-Egyptian Sudan
alt_names: Egyptian Sudan under Muhammad Ali and the Khedives

predecessors.note: Sennar fell 14-15 June 1821; the Shaigiya, the Ja'alin and Kordofan (Darfur) fell to the same invasion.

land.text: everything but Wadi Halfa and Suakin: "Kassala and Sennar fell soon after" Khartoum

successors.note: Khartoum fell 26 January 1885; Kassala and Sennar soon after (Mahdist State page).

land.text: Equatoria, held by Emin Pasha as an isolated Egyptian outpost until 1889

successors.note: Cut off by the Mahdists by 1883 (Equatoria page).
Left in Anglo-Egyptian hands at the end of 1885.

capitals.name: Khartoum
capitals.note: The conquest page: "May 1821: Khartoum becomes headquarters"; the Turkiyah page: "In 1823, Khartoum had become the centre of the Egyptian domains in Sudan" and "In 1835 Khartoum became the seat of the Hakimadar (governor general)". Before May 1821 the army moved with Ismail Pasha from Aswan.

correction.text: the Nile from Aswan to the Dongola reach: Ismail Pasha left Aswan on 20 July 1820 and beat the Shaygiya at Korti on 4 November

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (the colony has no Cliopatria row; Cliopatria draws the Muhammad Ali dynasty shape 1811-1821 at 0.60 M km2 reaching 15.2 N). The page gives no boundary or area.

correction.text: Dongola, Berber (submitted 5 March 1821), Sennar and the Gezira (14-15 June 1821) and Kordofan (Battle of Barah)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Muhammad Ali shape 1822-1833 is 1.64 M km2 to 10.9 N; the union of the Funj 1820 shape, Nubia and Kordofan is about 1.0-1.2 M km2. The pages give no area; the 10.9 N reach in Cliopatria is Fashoda and the Shilluk, which the pages date 1828 (reached) or 1855 (added).

correction.text: "In 1840, the regions of Kassala and Taka were added to the Egyptian domains"
Fashoda added (1855 on the conquest page)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Turkiyah page says Egyptian forces "reached Fashoda in 1828"; the conquest page lists Fashoda among later additions in 1855; the later date is used for annexation.

correction.text: "In 1865 the Ottoman Empire ceded the Red Sea coast and its ports to Egypt"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Suakin and Massawa are the ports; the page dates neither separately.

correction.text: Equatoria established by Samuel Baker in 1870

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Equatoria page also puts "northern parts of present-day Uganda, including Lake Albert and West Nile" in the province; no admin-1 names exist for those, so only South Sudan Equatoria is drawn.

New keyframe, the colony at its greatest extent. Cliopatria's Khedivate of Egypt shape 1877-1884 is 3.0 M km2 (to 1.9 N, 45.1 E, taking in Egyptian Somaliland); the pages opened give no Harar or Somali coast date, so those are not drawn here. Mahdist losses (Kordofan 1882, Darfur 1883) are ledger events inside the span.

correction.text: after the fall of Khartoum only Equatoria, Wadi Halfa and Suakin remained

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: "Kassala and Sennar fell soon after" Khartoum; only "Sawakin" and "Wadi Halfa" "remained in Anglo-Egyptian hands" by the end of 1885; Equatoria stayed out of Mahdist hands until 1889.

ledger.note: 20 July 1820: Muhammad Ali's son Ismail Pasha leads the army south from Aswan. "Ismail Kamil Pasha ... joined the roughly 4,000-strong force at Aswan on 20 July and led it south from Egypt"; the page names Aswan, not a border.

4 November 1820: the Shaygiya fall at Korti. "Egyptian firearms and artillery defeated the Shaygiya cavalry" (4 November) and destroyed their infantry on 2 December; the page does not date the conquest of Dongola itself.

region.text: Dongola and the Shaygiya country up to Korti

ledger.note: 1821: Kordofan falls after the Battle of Barah, where the Defterdar's army beat a larger Darfuri force. The page does not give the year of the battle explicitly (it follows the 1821 events), so 1821 is a bridge; the Turkiyah page says the forces "conquered Kurdufan".
5 March 1821: Berber submits to Ismail Pasha without a fight. The page does not say whose Berber was; the Funj dossier counts the Nile as far as Berber as Funj and Abdallab land.
May 1821: Khartoum becomes the army's headquarters and later Sudan's capital (the Turkiyah page dates its role as centre to 1823 and as the governor-general's seat to 1835).
14-15 June 1821: Sennar falls and the Funj sultanate ends. "Last Funj sultan Badi VII surrendered on 14 June, and the Egyptians occupied Sennar the next day."

region.text: Sennar and the Gezira, the Funj sultanate

ledger.note: Late 1822: Ismail Pasha is killed at Shendi and the Ja'alin rise. "Mek Nimr's Ja'alin confronted him over demands for money and slaves, they set fire to the house where he was sleeping"; garrisons were evacuated.
1823: the Defterdar restores Egyptian control by punitive campaigns. "Revolts and reconquest 1822-1823 ... about 30,000 killed according to the Funj Chronicle."

1840: Kassala and Taka are added to the Egyptian domains. "In 1840, the regions of Kassala and Taka were added to the Egyptian domains." Taka had been lost by the Funj in 1791 (Funj dossier) and had no state of its own.

1855: Fashoda is listed among the later additions. The Turkiyah page has the Egyptians reach Fashoda in 1828 ("They advanced southwards along the White Nile and reached Fashoda in 1828"); the 1855 date of the conquest page is used for annexation.
1865: the Ottoman Empire cedes the Red Sea coast to Egypt. "In 1865 the Ottoman Empire ceded the Red Sea coast and its ports to Egypt."

region.text: the Red Sea coast and its ports

ledger.note: 1870: Samuel Baker establishes Equatoria. "Equatoria was established by Samuel Baker in 1870"; Gordon took over in 1874 and Emin Pasha in 1878. The page puts the northern Ugandan lands in the province too.
1874: Darfur is conquered and annexed. "in 1874, conquered and annexed Darfur."

August 1881: the Mahdi's followers destroy two Egyptian companies on Aba Island. "Two Egyptian infantry companies sent to arrest Muhammad Ahmad fired on each other by mistake and were then destroyed by his followers"; a second force was ambushed on 9 December 1881. The page names the island, not the ground held.

1882: El Obeid starves into submission. "Early in 1882, the Ansar" overwhelmed a British-led Egyptian force near Al Ubayyid and the Mahdi besieged the town, "starving it into submission after four months"; the page gives no date for the surrender. The Mahdist War page has Hicks Pasha's army destroyed at El Obeid on 3-4 November 1883.
1883: Darfur is lost. "Slatin was captured in 1883," and "Mahdist forces soon took control of most of Darfur."
1885: Kassala and Sennar fall. "Kassala and Sennar fell soon after" the fall of Khartoum; the page gives no month.

1885: bridge for the rest of the Nile, Gezira and the White Nile. The page says only that by the end of 1885 "Sawakin" and "Wadi Halfa" "remained in Anglo-Egyptian hands"; the dates of the Berber, Dongola and Bahr el Ghazal losses are not on the pages opened.

region.text: the rest of the colony outside Wadi Halfa, Suakin and Equatoria

ledger.note: 1885: Equatoria is left as an isolated outpost. "By 1883 the Mahdists had cut off outside communications"; Emin Pasha, deposed by his officers in August 1887, held it until "The Mahdist Revolt put an end to Equatoria as an Egyptian outpost in 1889"; the split year follows the fall of Khartoum and is a bridge.

26 January 1885: with Khartoum the Egyptian government in Sudan ends, though the Mahdist War continues against Anglo-Egyptian forces to 1899 (Mahdist State dossier). The colony's contest with the Mahdists is closed here.
26 January 1885: Khartoum falls. "the city fell on 26 January 1885, after a siege of 313 days"; Gordon and the garrison were massacred.
January 1885: the Turco-Egyptian period ends. The page closes it with "the fall of Khartoum in 1885 to Muhammad Ahmad, the self-proclaimed Mahdi" (the date, 26 January, is on the Mahdist War page).

wars.name: Turco-Egyptian conquest of Sudan

zones.text: the Nile valley, Gezira and Kordofan

wars.outcome: "Turco-Egyptian victory": Dongola, Berber, Sennar and Kordofan taken in 1820-21, the Ja'alin revolt crushed in 1822-23.
wars.note: The page also lists Kassala (1840), Fashoda (1855), Suakin and the Red Sea coast (1865), Equatoria (1870) and Darfur (1874) as later additions.

wars.name: Mahdist War

zones.text: Kordofan, Darfur, Khartoum, Kassala and Sennar

wars.outcome: Mahdist victory: Kordofan 1882, Darfur 1883, Khartoum on 26 January 1885, Kassala and Sennar soon after; Wadi Halfa and Suakin stayed Anglo-Egyptian.
wars.note: The war runs to 1899 (Mahdist State dossier); only the years of this colony are given. Hicks Pasha's army was destroyed at El Obeid on 3-4 November 1883.

certainty.note: The Egyptian frontier on the Nile at Wadi Halfa and the Ethiopian and Equatorial limits are approximate; no source here gives a boundary line.

notes:
New dossier of type colony: Cliopatria has no row for the colony (its Egyptian shapes, muhammad-ali-dynasty 1811-1865 and khedivate-of-egypt 1866-1884, include Sudan: a rendering agent should draw this colony as the vassal tint of the Egyptian metropole and subtract it from the metropole's own shapes, or the land is drawn twice). The me-10 dossiers for the Muhammad Ali dynasty and the Khedivate should name this slug as counterpart for their Sudan events. Pages opened: Turkiyah (Turco-Egyptian Sudan), Turco-Egyptian conquest of Sudan (1820-1824), Equatoria, Mahdist War, Mahdist State (5, the budget).
Not on the pages: Wikipedia has no area figure for the colony; Bahr el Ghazal's annexation (the Turkiyah page says Equatoria, Bahr al Ghazal and Upper Nile were organised under Ismail with no years), Harar and the Somali coast (Egyptian occupation 1875-1885, not on the Turkiyah page; Cliopatria's Khedivate shape 1877-1884 reaches 1.9 N, 45 E and probably includes them), Massawa and Suakin's fall dates, Berber (26 May 1884) and Dongola. A gap-filler should open 'Egyptian Somaliland' / 'Emirate of Harar' and 'Siege of Khartoum'. The 1885 loss of the remainder is a confidence-1 bridge.
Counterparts needing dossiers: shaigiya ('Shaigiya (Shaykiyya)' string, also used by the Funj dossier), Ja'alin (Mek Nimr), equatoria-province (written in this batch). The Mahdist State dossier uses the counterpart string 'Equatoria Province' for its 1889 gain; it is this batch's equatoria-province.
Disagreement: Fashoda reached 1828 (Turkiyah page) or added 1855 (conquest page); Khartoum as centre 1821 (conquest page), 1823 or 1835 (Turkiyah page).
